Hon’ble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
None

5647/2017) stands disposed of.

Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Mr. Bharat Tewari, counsel for the 
appellant/Insurance Company.
2. Mr. Vinoda Nand Barthwal, counsel for 
the respondent nos. 1 to 4 in AO No. 386 of 
2017.
3. Mr. M. S. Bhandari, counsel for the 
respondent nos. 1 to 4 in AO No. 287 of 2017.
4. Counsel for the appellant in both the 
appeals would submit that in Appeal No. 386 
of 2017 only one witness was examined on 
behalf of the claimants before the Tribunal, 
however, she was not the eye witness of the 
incident and the Tribunal erred in appreciating
the evidence of the alleged witness in another 
M.A.C.T. No. 60 of 2015, which is under 
challenged in AO No. 287 of 2017. 
5. Counsel for the respondents seeks time to 
apprise himself with regard to the facts of the 
case including on the point that whether the 
M.A.C.T Petition No. 60 of 2015 and 
M.A.C.T Petition No. 70 of 2015 were 
clubbed together or not and place the case law 
before the Court on the next date fixed.
6. List these matters on 30.10.2023.
 (Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) 
 26.07.2023

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
AO No. 386 of 2017
With 
AO No. 287 of 2017
Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Present Mr. Bharat Tewari, counsel for 
the appellant/Insurance Company in both the 
appeals. 
Present Mr. Vinoda Nand Barthwal, 
counsel for the respondent nos. 1 to 
4/claimants in AO No. 386 of 2017. 
Present Mr. M. S. Bhandari, counsel for 
the respondent nos. 1 to 4/claimants in AO No. 
287 of 2017.
2. Counsel for the appellant would submit 
that no eye witness was examined before the 
Tribunal on behalf of the claimants; that, an 
evidence of Sandeep Naudiyal recorded in 
another claim petition arising out of the same 
accident was filed, but the same witness was 
not produced in the present claim petition and 
no opportunity was afforded to the 
appellant/Insurance Company to cross￾examine Sandeep Naudiyal in the present 
claim petition. 
He would further submit that the Motor 
Accident Claim Tribunal wrongly relied upon 
the certified copy of the statement of Sandeep 
Naudiyal in another claim petition without 
examining him in the present claim petition, 
hence, the impugned award is not sustainable. 
3. Counsel for the respondents/claimants 
prays for time to place the law on the point 
that such certified copy of the statement 
recorded in another case notwithstanding the 
absence of opportunity of examining that 
witness and cross-examining by the  appellant/Insurance Company is relevant can 
be read in evidence against the 
appellant/Insurance Company. 
4. Not objected to by the counsel for the 
appellant.
5. List this matter on 14.03.2024.
6. Let a copy of this order be kept in the 
connected appeal. 
 (Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) 
 30.10.2023
Akash
